approvalScope: Static style-direction comparison against the user's supplied visual reference. This is not approval of final runtime emotion mappings or animation assets.
method: Viewed the user's reference, both complete source sheets and the final 30-tile comparison. Compared eye construction, gaze, asymmetry and emotional gesture at source and contact-sheet sizes. Verified exact file hashes. Glow and stroke weight alone were not accepted as evidence of a new style.

directions.reference_glow: The rounded lid-and-cup eyes, asymmetric open and half-lidded pairs, upward-looking pupil cutouts and restrained cyan halo closely follow the supplied reference. Happy and Delighted use closed upward arches, while Quiet thought uses filled upward-looking eyes. The change is visible in the eye shapes even without considering glow.
directions.character: The stronger direction uses squashed filled eyes, large dark pupil cutouts, unequal eye height and different constructions within a pair. Quiet thought looks upward; Curious combines a tall eye with a low half-lid. These structural changes distinguish it from v2's contour and material variations.

faceNotes.result: Reference style reads friendly and relaxed. More expressive reads cheeky because of the half-lid and sideways gaze, and is close to that direction's Playful pose.
Both directions have an attentive open eye and small closed mouth. Strong eye asymmetry can also suggest curiosity; the label needs testing before runtime adoption.
Reference style reads skeptical or questioning. More expressive reads puzzled or confused, with a slight frown. Both are exploratory alternatives rather than exact neutral-curiosity matches.
Upward-looking pupil cutouts communicate thought more directly than the old neutral squint. This is a clear improvement against the reference criterion.
Closed smiling eyes communicate happiness in both directions; the reference direction has a larger open smile.
Asymmetric lid and open-eye pair with a curled smile reads playful. More expressive shares most of its eye construction with Calm.
Level half-lids and no mouth read more unimpressed or deadpan than the original closed arcs.
Reference style uses drooping lids and an oval mouth; More expressive uses closed eyes and a small yawn. Both retain a tired gesture.
Mouthless happy arches or squeezed chevrons retain the delighted role.
Drooping asymmetric lids, a frown and one tear clearly retain sadness in both directions.

limitations: The approval is for showing two static style directions to the user. Several expression labels remain interpretive, particularly Calm, Listening and Curious.
More expressive Calm and Playful are too similar to treat as clearly separated runtime emotions without further drawing changes.
The supplied reference includes activity symbols that help communicate state. Those symbols were intentionally omitted, so the face alone carries less task-specific meaning.
These studies have no newly tested blinks, transitions, speech mouths or voice synchronization. Pupil movement and the cyan halo need motion and small-screen testing before animation adoption.
Visual judgments are not a user study and do not establish that every viewer will read each expression identically.
